title: The Atlantic large-change frequency contrast changed sign with the domain in NOAA 2016-2025 upper-ocean fields
abstract: We tested whether total steric annual changes exceed fixed local thermal thresholds less often than thermal changes. We used NOAA upper-700-m fields. Local thermal 90th percentiles were set from centered annual changes in 2006-2015. Tests used 2016-2025. The total-minus-thermal area-weighted exceedance difference was 3.15 percentage points in the full Atlantic mask, with conditional 95% two-year block limits of 2.62 to 3.82. Between 60 S and 60 N, it was -1.60 points, with limits -2.33 to -0.77. Excluding thresholds below 10 mm gave -0.50 points, with limits -1.05 to 0.17. Full-mask Pacific and Indian differences were 1.26 and 4.25 points. The Atlantic total-to-thermal mean-square ratio was 0.699 despite more threshold exceedances. Small local thermal thresholds help explain this distinction between area-weighted energy and local-threshold frequency. The primary proposed frequency reduction was not supported in the full mask. Added domain checks limit the opposite broad claim. One mapped product, ten test years, fixed calibration thresholds, revised data and no coverage screen limit inference. Code, aggregate rates, source hashes, independent checks and figures are included. This test does not identify a physical cause or coastal hazard.

display.caption: Domain checks change the Atlantic exceedance contrast sign. Limits use paired two-year blocks and fixed calibration thresholds. Domain checks were added after the primary result.
Full-mask annual rates and conditional two-year block limits. The displayed excess does not persist across all domains.
